description:
A scanning electron microscope (SEM) image of a eutectic alloy has been corrupted by diagonal periodic noise (likely 60Hz interference). Your task is to restore the image using Frequency Domain (FFT) filtering in Fiji.

1. The noisy image is loaded at startup (~/Fiji_Data/raw/sem_noise/alloy_noisy.tif).
2. Use 'Process > FFT > FFT' to view the frequency spectrum.
3. Identify the specific bright 'stars' (spikes) in the spectrum that correspond to the periodic noise.
4. Mask/remove these spikes (e.g., using the brush tool or selection) without removing the central DC component or structural frequencies.
5. Perform the Inverse FFT to reconstruct the image.
6. Save the restored result to ~/Fiji_Data/results/sem_restoration/alloy_restored.tif.

The goal is to remove the stripes while preserving the sharp edges of the alloy microstructure. Do NOT simply apply a Gaussian blur.
